doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: De De's first job and forming his own band
summary: He got his first job replacing Cuckoo in a drummer's band, then branched out and formed his own groups.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, how did you come out on your first job? How did it happen you got a job?

Oh, let me see my first job. An old man, uh, fired me. I know of the past, he was a drummer. He played a lot of these furniture dancing all around St. Charles Street and all like that, you know. Oh yeah. And he had a son-in-law by the name of, who used to call him? That's when I was in New York. What's Cuckoo's right name back here, remember? Cuckoo?

Talbot, yeah. Well he was playing at that time with the past. And I didn't know they had a dissident in me. So, I know I heard my plan somewhere or another. And I joined his band in Cuckoo's place. And that was your first job? My first, a first, ain't a lot of them after. In other words, I stayed in their band. He's done a lot of work in this town. A lot of work. And they have his spots here in the city where they're in New York. I know what's the outside, you know, spots, you know. So I got my job. And I branched out from one fellow, hired me, a little band hired me. You know, hired me out like that, you know. Then I formed my own, one of them. I mean, one or two since then, you know, besides. And then I traveled a while. And then I got an old legend job, and I stayed there. And there were stuff I remember the Reese Corbett on sax, I can remember, myself, I think Wilhelmina Bart, she played at the time with me, piano, piano. Bass players, August Green, he's bass too, there was an old man at the time there, bass, I can remember. And afterwards, I kept Gus, myself, and I organized my own, because I remember my band for a time.

Yeah, he was an age of a man at the time. Of course I worked with Glenny also, you know, I hired Glenny on different jobs too, you know. I needed a band. So I said I played most of the old age I played with.
